Stomp Rocket Original Stunt Plane Refill - 1 Looper Plane Only - Performs Giant Loop - Gift for Boys or Girls Age 5+ Years Old - Active STEM Play Per my 6 year old: He loves his Stomp Rocket Stunt Planes because of being able to run, jump, and stomp on it. He also LOVES the green plane.

Per this mama: I bought this on Prime Day for a birthday gift for my son. I thought being able to run and jump for hours only to see a rocket pop up in the air would be worth every penny. Turns out I was right. The only downside is that I would not use this if you have small backyard. I live in the city, but I have fairly large yard. The rockets fly all over the place because they are stunt planes as opposed to rockets that are supposed to pop straight up into the sky. Think of the Stomp Rocket like a sewing machine. There's a pedal that you "stomp" to make the rocket go. Instead of electricity, air in the pedal flows into a tube and propels the rocket outward. The harder you stomp the higher it goes. The softer, then it doesn't go very far.

All of the planes are shaped differently and they each do different tricks. We haven't figured out all the best angles yet, but my son loves watching them go and then he runs after them. I would rather have just rockets because I hate having to traverse the poison ivy hill on the outskirts of my lawn, but you know whatever keeps the kids happy.
text_fidelity_b: Stomp Rocket Original Stunt Plane Refill - 1 Looper Plane Only - Performs Giant Loop - Gift for Boys or Girls Age 5+ Years Old - Active STEM Play

text_fidelity_a:
Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone This is so awesome and it works! I thought that with how affordable it is, that it wouldn't even be able to get off the ground, but it flies great! I have to warn you that it's super hard to fly, though. This will frustrate pretty much everyone except for someone who's already an expert in quad copters. But, it's an awesome first copter to practice on. I felt that I built my skills a lot with this, and now I can fly my bigger copter a lot better than I did before I played around with this.

An awesome thing about this is that you can separately order every part of this copter. And, unlike many electronic devices, the sum of the parts is about the same as getting a new one. So, I guess you could also just get two, and when one breaks, then fix it with the other one. Or wait for them to both break and then Frankenstein a whole one back together. But, because these have such available and interchangeable parts, then I can't give it less than five stars.

The battery lasts for about five minutes of flying. Or, fifteen minutes if you're like me, and get it stuck a lot. And, the blades are all plastic, but they hurt if they run into a person. This is also really easy to get stuck on top of a roof or in a tree, so I recommend flying it in a pretty open field. They do pretty good at crash landings, too, as long as they land on grass, which was most of my landings.

It is packaged with a bunch of replacement blades, too, so you don't have to worry about breaking a few of them. They're easy to replace, too.

This listing has both the CX-10 and CX10A. The only difference is that if you depress the left stick three times on the 10A, then you go into headless mode, which is better for beginners. If you want more control, though, then you should get the CX-10. Or, you should get both, since their parts are all interchangeable.
text_fidelity_b: Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone

Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

3Doodler Start Make Your Own HEXBUG Creature 3D Pen Set, Amazon Exclusive, with 2 Additional Insectoid DoodleMold First off, with the START, the main thing to know is it is safe. The temperature of the plastic and the pen tip is low enough, if you accidentally touch it, you won't get hurt. This is great for anyone who isn't fireproof.

It's a new skill. I'm an adult, and I got a bit on my finger the first time I tried it. I am grateful it's not the temperature of normal 3D printing filament (200-300C, and about in range of a soldering iron). With a regular pen, I'd have been in the emergency room. With this, I wiped it off and continued along. That ability, to learn and not worry that much about a beginner mistake, is exactly what attracted me to this. Think of it as training wheels.

The skill is transferable, so once you're confident with this, you can safely move on to the real deal. They make two other models to grow into, and those take pla and abs plastic.

What I didn't like was the lack of clear instructions. There is good stuff on their website, but a better manual would have been appreciated. That's my only ding. Otherwise, this was brilliant. They have additional kits over here [[ASIN:B01CL1FCEY 3Doodler Start Rocket & Robot DoodleBlock Kit]] not just the robot, but a page full of them, if you get tired of hexbugs.

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games UNO NFL LVII Card Game for Kids, Adults, Family and Game Night with Special "Touchdown" Rule for 2-10 Players Ok hear me out for a minute before I explain why I didn't give it a better rating. My wife and I love The Office. We consider ourselves huge fans-- buuut maybe not quite to the point of super fans because we can be forgetful on certain things about the show occasionally. But we are those people that, if you tell us a story, we'll likely have an Office reference to match it. So we were excited about getting to try this out.

This is where I might be a little too picky about it…well, I'm just going to say a little passionate about it lol. But if it's a classic game with a different theme (such as this one)-- it's usually directed toward people who are big fans of that specific theme...that likely will be expecting certain details. Otherwise, if they aren't fans, or real into that theme, they will probably just get the classic/original version...or go for a different theme that they are fans of. So if you're leaving big parts out, you're likely going to have some disappointed fans.

I also realize that there's so much great things about the show and so I'm sure it's hard to narrow it all down to a select amount of cards. So I give some credit to that.

My reasons for rating it lower:

Nearly all of the cards are of Michael, Dwight, Jim and Pam. Then there's randomly one of Kelly and the special rule/twist card with Kevin....but no one else is part of the game?! And yes, the ones included are amazing actors/characters and all...but many of the other regulars are, too- and all together they made The Office.

There are cards for numbers 0-9 (they each have the different colors) and 6 action cards. So that's 16 different pictures they could utilize. Which means there are enough to feature the regular characters…I'll list/count out the ones that come to my mind 1-Michael, 2-Dwight, 3-Jim, 4-Pam, 5-Angela, 6.Kevin, 7-Oscar, 8-Creed, 9-Meredith, 10-Stanley, 11-Phyllis, 12-Kelly, 13-Ryan, 14-Toby, 15-Darryl.

I also felt like some of the photos could have been better selected. I won't rant on too much about that, and spare you, but a quick example-- Kevin's chili twist card isn't of that actual scene just him at his desk. And why not put Toby as the draw 4 card, instead 😄

I do like the picture of the back-side of the cards, the wild card with Michael dancing in the Diwali episode and *some* of the other pics they chose.

The card and photo quality is really good. My box container was torn a little at the top.

It is still fun to play, I do like the special rule/twist for Kevin's chili, and like the idea of The Office theme but I do think it could be improved upon by including more characters.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games UNO NFL LVII Card Game for Kids, Adults, Family and Game Night with Special "Touchdown" Rule for 2-10 Players

text_fidelity_a:
Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+ Initially I bought Snap-Circuits for my 4 and 5 year old boys. I found the collection of capacitors, resistors, integrated circuit modules, and transistors was a little too abstract, and I was thinking I really wanted more stuff like electro-magnets, relays, motors, generators, switches, potentiometers, and maybe resistive loads like light bulbs and diodes -- more basic electrical stuff, of which there's some in the circuit kits but not a lot.

My boys are 5 and 6 now. I added Snaptricity to our collection of mostly unexplored Snap-Circuits, and suddenly they're creating all kinds of basic circuits with switches, buttons, lights, motors, and electro-magnets. They're starting to understand the flow of electricity, polarity, magnetism, and resistance (as they add more loads to their circuits). I've set the transistors and stuff aside for now, because there's tons of stuff to do with these more basic components first. For older children, they might be ready for the electronic components sooner, but with my younger kids, these electrical parts are great.

We do not follow the instructions. So it helps to have extra components on hand instead of the minimum number required for the book experiments. Some of our circuits are more than elegant and minimalist. I recommend buying two kits, or this kit and another one like the 100 or 300.

The brilliant thing about these components is the incredibly simple and effective button snap-connectors. The only downside to these components is they are encased in plastic for durability. The plastic is clear so the internal components can be seen. This is really a good thing, but it's worthwhile to have a coil/electromagnet that is un-encased, as well as a speaker/microphone (electromagnet with a diaphragm) that is not encased, and a motor that can be disassembled/dissected.
text_fidelity_b: Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+

Nature Bound Ant Treehouse Habitat Kit with Sand, Connector Tube, Feeding Stick & Insect Instructions, One Size This ant home(tree house) is much smaller than I was expecting, but it's not tiny. Make sure you look at the measurements, though, so your little ones aren't disappointed.

This comes with great directions, so you're led through what you need to do. You can order ants, but the directions are clear for if you chose to collect your own. The kit comes with a coupon to get cheaper ants. (I can't imagine anyone wanting ants bad enough to pay almost $20 for them.) The coupon and the first order page on the website says you'll get 5-10 ants, but then the main page says 30. Even with the coupon code, you're still paying $9.95 for ants(shipping IS included in that price). I can't pay that much when ants are in such abundance around our home. Again, though, I DO give them credit for the great directions for just using ants from the yard. You aren't expected to buy the ants, but you do have that option. Also, to make it clear, you won't get a queen ant if you order. You'll only get non-reproductive ants. (That information is from the website page for ordering the ants.)

It only took my boys a few minutes to come running with more than enough ants to fill their new little home. Unfortunately, our ants have been very slow to feel at home. One died, though we followed directions exactly. They aren't working together like I thought they would, either. That said, so far it has been greatly exciting to watch what little they have done. One ant looks like Goliath upside the other ants, so he's been easier to watch. It's surprisingly fascinating to watch ants move sand around! I assume there will be more efforts from the other ants with time, but I was expecting quicker results. (I don't blame that on the ant farm, by any means!)

One other complaint is the fact that the bottom goes on so loosely. I kept working with it thinking it should be tighter, but had no luck. This is something that will be best watched without too much handling from children, since there are 4 pieces that are easily removed. This kit comes with a tube, which can connect to another tree house if you chose to buy more. (The 2 side pieces can be removed for this connection.)

Overall, this is a fun kit for kids, but it could have been better designed. Every child needs to have the joy of watching ants work, though! ;)
text_fidelity_b: Nature Bound Ant Treehouse Habitat Kit with Sand, Connector Tube, Feeding Stick & Insect Instructions, One Size

Animoodles Magnetic Hazel Sloth Stuffed Animal Plush, 7.5" , Brown Many stuffed plush toys that are equipped with joints are difficult to pose. Using magnets in the place of joints makes posing your stuffie very easy. There are currently 14 different Animoodles Magnetic Stuffed Animal Plush toys. Most popular animals among today's current toy trends are available. The plush material is incredibly soft and the embroidered features are incredibly cute. We were able to have Kylie the Cat join our household. Her limbs were each held into place with a plastic tab, which was not difficult to clip and remove completely.

Kylie came with a booklet that tells the origin story of the Animoodles with small written profiles and photos of each toy in the series. There are also practical safety warnings regarding the magnets used in the plush.

I had some concerns about magnets in a child's toy, but the smallest magnet I can feel through the fabric is about the size of a nickle. The stitching is solid, it would be difficult to remove the magnets. Kylie has a lemon bow stitched onto her head, the colors are very cohesive. The pupil of the eyes are buttons. I would strongly advise this toy to not be available to any child under 3 or any other children that are prone to putting random objects into their mouth or being overly destructive with their toys. The button eyes and internal magnets are simply not safe for babies, toddlers or destructive children, as it's made clear in the attached booklet.

The Animoodles Magnetic Stuffed Animal Plush would make a great gift for many children. However, Kylie was in a sealed plastic bag inside the shipping box, so this may be a gift that is better to present in a gift bag rather than wrapping unless you opt to use the shipping box. Play would be expanded with more Animoodles from the series. Additional Animoodles allow for any sort of crazy plush hybrid desired.

My favorite features of the Animoodles is the creative construction and the softness of the plush material. This would make a great addition to any plush animal collection.

Adora Amazing Girls 18 Doll, Sienna (Amazon Exclusive) This is a beautiful girl and of really nice quality. I really like the face sculpt so much more than the Target Our Generation dolls and the soft body makes her a pleasure to hold. We do not have any American girl dolls in our home, but based on my memory of holding a friends, these seem a little more comparable in quality level to American girl than the cheaper our generation and 14 inch glitter girls which is what we have had in our home until now.

Her styling is beautiful, much more so in person than in the images. The longsleeve shirt is sparkly gold and kind of fits like a tunic top, and the black leggings are soft, shiny, and have some wonderful sparkle to them. The jacket and boots are a lovely soft fabric that is not loud and wrinkly, but rather smooth and pliable and lovely to the touch. The fur details are quite nice and do not seem to be depositing over much fuzz on the rest of her outfit. The boots are fabric and are relatively easy to get on, with a Velcro closure. Her little bag has an open top and is easy to set a few things inside of, though it is on the smaller side.

Curls are absolutely gorgeous! I did a little finger combing and gentle fluffing and she just looks so beautiful. Her skin tone is more of an olive skin tone than a cocoa color. I am white with blonde hair and blue eyes, and you can see my hand in some of the images next to the girls skin tone so that you can get a feeling of what her skin tone really looks like. To me she definitely reads as an African-American girl, but with a lighter skin tone.

I'm not a huge fan of the pale pink box that this line of dolls comes in because it doesn't seem modern, and seems more suited to a baby doll than something for an older girl, but the doll itself once you remove her from the box is lovely. If you are giving this doll as a special gift, consider taking her out of the box before giving, unclip her from the things holding her in, put on her shoes, and remove the hair net that is knotted quite tightly into her beautiful hair. The hairnet is protective of her hair in travel, but they tied it in with the thick piece of thread right at her forehead and even without an excited child sitting right there, I found it took me a number of minutes to carefully cut that off of her hair to free her gorgeous curls.

One other thing that I really like is that we have a boy doll from our generation, and I really appreciate whenever the clothes from girl dolls have parts that can be unisex enough for the dolls to share among themselves. This is really nice because these are just like regular clothes the real girl would wear, only a little bit fancy and dressed up. And our boy doll could certainly wear some of these pieces as well. She fits the other 18 inch doll clothing that we have from our generation and other brands and seems to be the standard 18 inch doll size.

Overall this is a high quality doll who is beautifully detailed, has lovely eyes which close when she lays down, and beautiful hair and clothing.
text_fidelity_b: Adora Amazing Girls 18 Doll, Sienna (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Blocks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler, and they have soft parts! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. I had almost forgotten about this little loom -- I first learned how to make these potholders in the 1950s even before I started school (I was probably 5 yrs old). My brother and I spent many summers working on these and selling them around the neighborhood to augment our $0.25/week allowance. My mother taught us how to make them and kept us supplied with the loops while we came up with our own designs.

One thing I remember very clearly -- she avoided nylon loops, preferring instead cotton loops. Why? Because the nylon loops could melt at the temperatures commonly encountered when using cast iron pans and metal baking dishes in hot ovens. I retained that memory, so when I saw this kit available with cotton loops, I knew I needed to try it one more time.

The major difference I see is in the length of the "prongs" in the loom -- I recall them being a little longer. Also, the metal weaving hook was a bit longer. But other than that, the design and construction are close to what I used as a child.

The package from Amazon arrived earlier today, and I quickly put together the potholder in the photo. It took probably an hour -- perhaps a bit longer, but not much. There are enough loops for a couple of pot holders and enough colors to mix and match. Follow the directions, especially the part about finishing -- pulling one of the loops on each finished edge back over a loom peg to keep the rest of the loops on the adjacent and opposite sides from popping off the loom. Take your time with this part -- it's easy to want to hurry to finish it, but it can be a bit "fiddly."

Very happy with this -- I've already ordered additional loops in specific colors to coordinate with my kitchen colors so I can make several of these to use as potholders as well as hot pads/trivets.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

LEGO Juniors/4+ Jurassic World Pteranodon Escape 10756 Building Kit (84 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This summer was the year of Jurassic World! My 5 turning 6 year old is too young to watch any of the Jurassic Park movies, but that didn't stop the advertisements and displays in stores from reaching audiences far and wide including my son. He already loves Legos AND dinosaurs so this was the perfect mashup for him! We already have other Lego Juniors sets (I honestly wish they would make more).

Lego Juniors are designed for 4-7 year olds. Basically, they are the same as the other Lego kits, but the instructions are more simplistic than the other kits for older children. The Legos designs are also more simple than the Lego kits for older children. The Legos are still the same size as regular Legos, so these are not an in between Duplos and Legos. If you step on them they will hurt. In addition, the pieces are tiny enough to get lost forever.

My son is a free form builder, he does not care about the actual instructions, what he cares about is the potential for creating what is shown on the package. His Lego bin is filled with Lego kits all mixed together and he has a blast creating his own world, which is limitless. So, if you are insistent on your child following the directions to a T, then I would not recommend these for a younger child. Most boys under 6 just do not have the patience for this. Frustration sets in quick and the desire to just play take over. Stick to Duplos or just plain free build sets until about age 6 or 7 if you want to stick to the instructions. However, if you don't mind the kits getting mixed up for creative play and you child loves Legos and Dinos, then this is the set for you.

As usual, the Legos are of the same quality we had when we were kids. I would recommend getting several of the Lego tools because some of this pieces are tiny and get stuck. The only way to get them out is via the Lego Tool!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Juniors/4+ Jurassic World Pteranodon Escape 10756 Building Kit (84 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Puzzle 1000 Pieces Adult - Puzzle 1000 Puzzle for Adults - De Haar Castle, Netherlands - Jigsaw Puzzles 1000 Pieces for Adults This GLISTELLO 1000-PIECE JIGSAW PUZZLE FOR ADULTS - DE HAAR CASTLE, NETHERLANDS (27.5 x 19.7 inches) is a good quality puzzle, highly appropriate for jigsaw puzzle experts. It has many similar cloud and tulip pieces that present a challenge to assembly, because the pieces need to be placed by shape as well as by color. Of course, jigsaw puzzle experts love these difficult jigsaws!

The puzzle pieces are small, which makes the 1000-piece puzzle fit easily on a worktable. The fully interlocking pieces are thick enough to be handled easily, and the interlocking tabs don’t bend if the pieces are handled with ordinary care. The pieces don’t click together like Ravensburger puzzle pieces, but they fit together unmistakably by feel when properly joined.

Unfortunately, the pieces don’t fit tightly enough to allow joined sections to be picked up and moved without falling apart. Completed sections need to be picked up on a sheet of paper, or pushed along the tabletop, to reach their proper locations in the puzzle.

The puzzle picture looks exactly like the photograph on the product page. The picture is nicely printed on the puzzle itself, and on a big sheet packed inside the box for reference during assembly. The price (about $19 on Amazon) is very reasonable for a jigsaw puzzle of this size and quality.

I wouldn’t recommend this puzzle for group assembly, because of the many pieces that are visually similar in color and shape. Puzzles like this one require a lot of sorting of pieces in advance by color and shape if the actual assembly is to proceed quickly.
text_fidelity_b: Puzzle 1000 Pieces Adult - Puzzle 1000 Puzzle for Adults - De Haar Castle, Netherlands - Jigsaw Puzzles 1000 Pieces for Adults

Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers Dance Champs 2pk - BUNNY PACK Kids often like toys best that offer movement of some kind. Flashing lights and sounds also have a certain appeal, but at the very least there needs to be some type of moving action. Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers is a toy that offers some action and many youngsters will take to this toy right away once they learn how it works.

Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers includes one pink and one purple bunny. To get the dancers dancing, all you do is insert one of the plastic slides into the bunny, then pull it out quickly. This gets the pointer on the base spinning fast. Like a top, you then place it on a smooth, flat surface and let it spin. The toy offers Mechanical operation, so no batteries are needed.

Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers are action- oriented and I was surprised by how long the dancers continue to spin like a top after a single pull from the plastic slide. Provided you pull the slide out quickly, the dancers will continue spinning for a while. One game my kids like is to spin both of them at the same time, then sit back and see whose bunny is spinning the longest. They have come up with a few other creative games also, and this surprised me a little at first because the toy seems so simple.

My girls find this toy amusing, but one thing I noticed is that, unlike their other toys, Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers has little staying power. That is, the spinning just isn't enough to keep my kids interested for long. At first, it seemed like fun watching the bunnies spin and making up games but after the first week, their interest had tapered off considerably. The simplicity of the toy is nice and I am grateful that it takes no batteries, but after one week, the bunnies have already been relegated to the bottom of the toy box.

Kids like toys that move, but apparently a toy that spins and does little else just doesn't have enough action to matter. I still find the Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers good enough to recommend a little, but I can understand why some people will rate this toy below average. Kids love it at first, but their interest falls rapidly once they realize how little these bunnies can actually do.
text_fidelity_b: Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers Dance Champs 2pk - BUNNY PACK

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5 This is a precious little game that I imagine young children will long remember.

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Overall, this is a very cute game, and I highly recommend it for little ones just learning to play games!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5

text_fidelity_a:
Lost Cities - The Board Game Lost Cities TBG is a lot like the original Lost Cities Card Game, but it supports more than 2-players. That's a nice feature.

For those who don't know, Lost Cities the Card Game is considered legendary among hobby board gamers because it's simple, but deep, meaning that anyone can pick up the rules to the game quite quickly, but there's interesting decision-making and complex outcomes to worry about based on your decisions. Of course, it's only a 2-player game, which can be a downfall for many.

The Board Game version is similar in terms of gameplay. If you've already experienced the card game, I could teach you this version in about 30 seconds. Unfortunately, you'll soon want to be back playing the card game. This game lacks a certain something to make it really fun. It works, and it's still easy to learn and play, but I don't think I'll come back to it all that often unless I'm playing with my daughter. For those who are into more complex games, this one just feels...old fashioned. In all the ways that the card game has aged well, this one hasn't.
text_fidelity_b: Lost Cities - The Board Game
